messages.task:
You are a financial data specialist who can call a set of high-level tools to inspect a synthetic finance database and perform calculations.

Scenario
A company report contains a “stock performance” graph that compares the cumulative total shareholder return of a $100 investment made on December 31 2010 (with dividends reinvested) in three entities:
 • O’Reilly Automotive Inc. (a company)
 • the S&P 500 Retail Index (an index)
 • the S&P 500 (an index)
The graph shows the value of that initial $100 investment at several year-end dates.

Available tools – you can invoke any of them as needed:
1. get_entity_id_by_name(name:str) → int | None
   Return the internal numeric identifier that the database uses for the given company or index name.
2. get_metric_value(entity_id:int, date_label:str, metric:str) → float | None
   Retrieve the numeric value recorded for the desired metric (e.g. "cumulative_total_return") for a specific entity and report-date label.
3. compute_roi(start_value:float, end_value:float) → float
   Compute the raw return-on-investment percentage between two numeric values.
4. format_percentage(value:float) → str
   Convert a numeric percentage to the nearest whole number followed by the “%” sign.
5. list_all_entities() → list[str]
   Get the names of every entity contained in the database.
6. get_entity_type(name:str) → str | None
   Discover whether a given name is stored as a “company” or an “index”.
7. list_date_labels_for_year(year:int) → list[str]
   Return every stored date-label that belongs to the specified calendar year.

Question
What is the ROI of an investment in the O’Reilly Automotive Inc. from 2010 to 2011?

Use the tools to find or derive the answer and respond with exactly the ROI as a percentage string (for example: 25%).
